purpose: Compliance matrix consumed by Vizzie to (a) decide whether a dataset may be ingested, (b) render required attribution on maps, embeds and exports, (c) set per-portal crawl rates.

ingest_policy_values.allow: Ingest and serve normally with attribution.
ingest_policy_values.allow_with_flag: Ingest, but surface a share-alike warning to the user before export/publish.
ingest_policy_values.link_only: Do NOT ingest. Show metadata and link to the source portal.
ingest_policy_values.block: Do not surface for ingest at all.

resolution_order: 1. Dataset-level licence from the portal API (normalised via licence_aliases).
2. If absent/unmappable -> portal.default_licence (only where the portal publishes a blanket licence).
3. If still absent -> UNDECLARED (ingest policy: link_only).
usage.attribution: Render licences[<id>].attribution_template with {title} {publisher} {retrieved}. Attribution is non-removable at every tier for the SOURCE; only Vizzie branding is removable.

PUBLIC-DOMAIN.name: Public domain (publisher declaration)
PUBLIC-DOMAIN.attribution_template: {title} — {publisher}, released into the public domain. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
PUBLIC-DOMAIN.note: A publisher's bare 'Public Domain' declaration, which is the single most common licence value on the Socrata network (260 of 911 sampled datasets, 15 Sep 2026 — NYC, Seattle and CDC all use it). Deliberately its own class rather than an alias of US-PD or CC0-1.0: US-PD is specifically the 17 USC §105 federal-works carve-out and does not describe a city portal, and CC0 is a specific legal instrument the publisher did not necessarily execute. This class claims only what the publisher actually said — no rights reserved — so attribution is not required, though the template still offers one.

SEMCOG-CLA.name: SEMCOG Copyright License Agreement
SEMCOG-CLA.attribution_template: {title} — Copyright © SEMCOG. All Rights Reserved. Reproduction or Use Without Permission is Prohibited. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
SEMCOG-CLA.note: A bespoke agreement, read in full 2026-09-19, covering everything on SEMCOG's Hub: clause 1(a) grants a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use, reproduce, modify, distribute, publish, transmit, display and create derivative works, so it is more permissive than its name suggests and commercial use is not restricted. The condition is clause 2(a): every use must carry the copyright notice verbatim, in a reasonably prominent position — which is why this is a class with a fixed attribution_template rather than UNDECLARED. The agreement's example notice carries a year ('Copyright © 2019 SEMCOG'); the template omits it because the year belongs to the work, not the retrieval, and SEMCOG does not publish a per-dataset copyright year. Clause 1(b) excludes third-party rights, so a dataset SEMCOG merely redistributes is not covered by this grant.

OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL.name: Open Government Licence – Canadian province or municipality
OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL.attribution_template: Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – {publisher}. Retrieved {retrieved} via Vizzie.
OGL-CA-PROVINCIAL.note: Alberta, British Columbia, Ontario, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick and Yukon each publish their own Open Government Licence, all modelled on the federal OGL 2.0. Ontario's text was read in full (19 Sep 2026) as the family exemplar: reuse for any lawful purpose, explicitly including commercial purposes, conditional on acknowledging the source and linking the licence. The other five rest on open.canada.ca's own licence register, which gives each one's official title and URL; Alberta's and Yukon's pages 403 a server fetch and were not read. One class rather than six because they differ only in the licensor, and the attribution wording each mandates — 'Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence – <licensor>' — is exactly what {publisher} fills in. ~10,500 datasets (19 Sep 2026). Deliberately NOT here: Manitoba's OpenMB Information and Data Use License and Saskatchewan's SUUDL, which are different instruments rather than OGLs, and Vancouver's and Toronto's municipal licences, whose texts are still unreachable — see the resolve.test.ts case that keeps them UNDECLARED.

rate_limit.note: 20 requests per minute, and ADB BANS rather than throttles: exceed it and every path on the host (structure endpoints included) returns HTTP 403 text/html reading "You have been temporarily banned." for roughly 15 minutes, with no Retry-After. Measured 2026-09-12. Useful ground truth: every response carries x-ratelimit-limit: 20 and x-ratelimit-remaining, and the bucket refills on a ~60s window (observed 15 -> 20 after 65s); there is no x-ratelimit-reset. 0.25 req/s = 15/min leaves headroom, because one ingest costs TWO requests (the HEAD size probe plus the GET) and a ban is expensive to recover from. HEAD returns no content-length here, so that probe buys nothing from this portal - worth skipping outright if the budget ever gets tight. ADB's own docs contradict themselves on the number (the v5 page says 30/min, two other places say 20); the headers say 20, so 20 it is.

rate_limit.note: No published per-second limit. The real constraint is extraction size, not rate: past a size the server estimates from the dataflow's key space, data queries 413 (EXTRACTION_TOO_BIG, max 5,000,000 rows) or return HTTP 200 with a SOAP envelope queueing an async job (measured 2026-09-15: 40k obs streams, 120k queues). The connector filters its catalogue to <= 50k observations for this reason.

portals.tos_note: SPC governs the hub; licences are carried per dataset and vary enormously. The hub is a harvester — it restates the licence of the source portal (SPC GeoNode, data.gouv.nc, SPREP), so resolution must be per dataset, never per portal.

rate_limit.note: No published limit. 2 req/s is the conservative CKAN default. The catalogue API lives under the /data prefix; the bare pacificdata.org/api path sits behind Cloudflare and returns an interstitial.

portals.notes: 14,393 datasets, 84% of them PDF — a library catalogue with a data catalogue inside it. 901 datasets carry a geospatial resource (710 GeoJSON, 425 shapefile variants, 571 WMS). Licence-wise the Pacific default is CC BY-NC-SA: 403 of those 901 are non-commercial and blocked. The commercially ingestable geo set is ~266, of which 217 are New Caledonia under LO-2.0. Measured 10 Sep 2026.
